presentation.label: 128 arrangements per project
presentation.summary: 16 books of 8 arrangements per project, every one a stock arrangement file: book 1 is arr01 to arr08, book 16 is arr121 to arr128.
presentation.overview: Songbook turns the Octatrack's 8 arrangements into 16 books of 8. Book 1 is stock's own arr01 to arr08 and stays exactly as it is; book 2 is arr09 to arr16, and so on up to arr128, all ordinary stock arrangement files in the project folder, written and read by the Octatrack's own code. In ARR > CHANGE, with the transport stopped, LEFT and RIGHT step through the books; inside a book every stock arrangement function works as usual. Setlists of up to 16 songs from any books follow in a later version.
highlights: Every arrangement is a stock file, arr01 to arr128.
Switch books with LEFT/RIGHT in ARR > CHANGE, stopped.
A project opens on book 1, also on a unit without the module.
usage: Open ARR > CHANGE (MKII: ARR, then CHANGE; MKI: FUNC + PATTERN for arrangement mode, FUNC + BANK, then CHANGE), with the transport stopped.
Press RIGHT or LEFT to step to the next or previous book (1 to 16); BOOK 2 and so on shows at the top right.
Pick one of the book's 8 arrangements as usual and edit, save or chain it: stock's arrangement functions work inside the book.
Save the project as usual: every book is saved with it.
Before removing the module, step back to book 1.

limitations: OS 1.40C, tested on an MKI (the developer's own checks: books on build b976e98ff, setlists on build 7a53e26af, base 0.7.13); not tested on an MKII.
Books change only while the transport is stopped: the switch writes and reads the card, which stock itself does only stopped.

Switch back to book 1 before removing the module: without it, stock's next save writes the book in use into arr01 to arr08. Book 1 is kept in a backup (arr01.bak to arr08.bak) and comes back the next time the module is installed and book 1 is chosen.
A project comes back to the book and arrangement it was saved or left on; a power cycle keeps the book in use. Without the module a project opens on book 1.
Stock's project copy functions copy book 1 only; copying the project folder copies every book.

Setlists borrow the open book's arrangements 7 and 8 while they play; end a setlist (open ARR > BOOKS) before removing the module, or stock's next save writes the setlist's copies into those two arrangements.
Edits made while a setlist plays are written when it ends; a RELOAD or power cycle before that drops them, as stock drops unsaved changes.

tests.summary: Host gate (verify.py, 218 checks: books, backups, failed reads, reloads; setlists: playing through stock's CHAIN, the end, editing during a show, copy/paste, names, the main-screen and title displays, and every path that can touch slots 7 and 8: reload, power cycle, reinstall, stock refilling them); ot_emu captures of the menu, page, window and main screen and a SAVE/RELOAD reproduction. On the developer's MKI (OS 1.40C, base 0.7.13, beside USB AUDIO and Arr Rows): books through the test procedure (build b976e98ff); setlists playing through with gapless changes, the next song chosen live, copy/paste, names, the displays, an edit during a show saved to its song, and returning into the setlist after RELOAD and a power cycle with the songs intact (build 7a53e26af), as the developer reported them. Two data-loss faults found on the unit during this work are fixed and covered by host tests that fail on the faulty code (TESTING.md).

steps: Open ARR > BOOKS (MKII: ARR, then BOOKS; MKI: FUNC + PATTERN for arrangement mode, FUNC + BANK, then BOOKS), with the transport stopped.
Press RIGHT or LEFT to step to the next or previous book (1 to 16); BOOK 2 and so on shows at the top right. Arrangements work inside the book as in stock.
Press CUE + YES on an arrangement to add it to the open setlist (LIST 1 at the bottom right).
Open SETLSTS in the Arranger menu, put the cursor on the first song and press YES, close the menu and press PLAY: each song follows the last.
Open ARR > BOOKS, stopped, to end a setlist; end it and step back to book 1 before removing the module.
